features.note: Ears now carry 4 mounting holes (two per ear at the EIA-310 0.625 in vertical pitch) — a flange without a hole cannot receive a screw, and receiving a screw is the whole claim of this critical.

Each of the 9 module bays now has an EXTRACTION HANDLE and is separated by a BAY DIVIDER (the chassis wall between bays). Confirmed in a brightened crop: a row of handle bars with vertical dividers between them. The handle is what makes a hot-swap bay read as a bay (a module must come OUT) and it is the only relief available on a 349 px band; the dividers stop the 9 slots reading as 9 faces on a continuous plate.
3 PSU bays with their own handles and dividers, distinct from the module bank.
RJ45 cage/throat and the alarm dry-contact block read (the alarm block on the left of the brightened band). No invented count/type.
Livery placeholder intact; no ratings anywhere; provenance still surfaced in the HUD.

important_features.note: Mounting holes reinforce the rack-mount read.

defects: ABSOLUTE EXPOSURE (correctly deferred to materials/lighting, NOT a structural defect): 3 of 4 front surfaces render at the tone-curve FLOOR (chassis front 0.042, module face 0.103, PSU 0.074 on 0..1), where discrimination is nearly gone. This is why the front furniture reads subtly — and it is a THIRD property (absolute exposure) that size and relative-contrast checks are blind to (all pairs already clear 20% Weber; a module face is 124 px, not too small). Materials (chassis colour is UNDOCUMENTED, so lightening is available) and the front-favouring lighting rig own this, with the numbers now recorded.
Tightest pair to resolve: PSU face vs module face at 28% Weber — separating the two banks is exactly what lets a viewer count them.
Emissive intensity 4.0 still SEEDED from the Axis, unmeasured against this housing (re-measure through the curve in lighting).
corrections: Materials: lift the chassis exposure off the curve floor (undocumented colour permits it) and separate the PSU vs module banks; measure THROUGH the tone curve, not linear.
Lighting: favour the front like the UPS/Axis; re-measure the LED intensity against this housing.

mechanical.notes: 6/6 suites. 81 meshes / 2128 tris. Console clean. THE STANDOUT is the diagnosis: my 'reads subtly' note was decomposed into three INDEPENDENT measurable properties that an impression cannot separate, and measured — SIZE (module face 124 px, divider 16.7 px, LED 20 px: not the problem; the real constraint is the whole 1U band is 349 px tall), RELATIVE CONTRAST (every adjacent pair clears 20% Weber: module-vs-cavity 99%, PSU-vs-module 28%: not the problem), and ABSOLUTE EXPOSURE (3 of 4 fronts at the curve floor: THE problem). Weber is a RATIO — it says two surfaces differ, never that both are near-black; two blacks 59% apart are still two blacks. That diagnosis decided the fix belongs to materials/lighting, so structural did NOT mis-repair it by enlarging pieces. What structural DID: functionally-forced relief — extraction handles (a hot-swap module must come out), bay dividers (the chassis wall, else 9 faces on one plate), and 4 ear mounting holes — none inventing a count or type the evidence is silent on (the line that separates it from the UPS rear receptacles). GUARD verifyBaysAreComplete: each populated bay needs its face, handle, LED, and exactly one of {module, blank} — counts CANNOT see a handle floating over a blank plate (every piece count stays correct, only the per-bay SET is wrong), the floating-piece failure disguised as a state toggle; negative control: hiding bay 0's handle fires it once, 0 as built in both module states. Verified: counts (9 handles, 3 PSU handles, 8 dividers, 2 PSU dividers, 4 holes), 0 incomplete bays in all+partial (handle follows the module, never the blank), 0 floating, framing/lighting unchanged, boot clean.

notes: Inline orchestrator judgment. The pass's discipline is the point: rather than take my 'front reads subtly' at face value, the builder decomposed it into size / relative-contrast / absolute-exposure, measured all three, and found the real cause is absolute exposure — a materials-and-lighting property, NOT a structural one — so it deliberately did not 'fix' it by enlarging geometry, and recorded the numbers for the passes that own it. That is exactly how a pass avoids mis-solving another's problem, and it extends the Axis tone-curve lesson (Weber is a ratio; it is blind to both-near-black). The relief it did add is real and functionally forced (handles, dividers, mounting holes) with no invented counts, guarded by a bay-completeness check with a negative control that catches the count-invisible floating-handle failure. Cleared to the materials pass, where the exposure gets fixed with the numbers already in hand.
